name: manual_68237f
claim: When supervising child processes through HTTP loopback proxies under spend bounds, enforce five structural patterns: (1) admit and count each connection synchronously in process_request before spawning its handler thread; (2) a three-phase lifecycle RUNNING -> DRAINING -> CLOSED, where stop_and_drain shuts down the accept loop, waits on a condition variable for admitted handlers and sets CLOSED only on timeout, and every upstream dispatch first claims a slot under the same lock, so no claim succeeds after CLOSED although a request claimed before it may still be sent (the launcher then exits 124); (3) two outcomes for every forwarded chat request, ACCOUNTED (identity-encoded 2xx with verified completion usage) or UNACCOUNTED (everything else, including every non-2xx status and every transport or read failure), the latter debited the whole clamp and ending fail-closed with exit 124, with no status trusted as a zero-spend rejection; (4) clamp max_tokens and max_completion_tokens to the remaining budget before forwarding; (5) authenticate the child with a random per-launch session token. On distributed task queues keep claimed_at fencing tokens strictly increasing per task; a takeover completes only with --expected-claimed-at.

decisions.notes: Corrects lesson_de193e76f558, which still described a trusted definitive-rejection class and an accepting flag. Checked against the cline-wandb launcher package at orama-system fb28125e (proxy_handler.py, proxy_server.py, accounting.py) and PHASE_TRACKING.md in Perpetua-Tools 4bcbf5d4.
